_comment: MACAW II, single-port — Kingston AE5028 2024-25 team build (RTC project manager). Forty-three placed instances become eighteen parts. Names come from the CAD part names, which are the team's own functional labels: Plate_nozzle_retainer, Plate_oxidiser_manifold and so on. Nothing here is inferred about what a plate does. A pattern is 'owner/model' or bare 'model'; first match wins. Every placed instance must match a rule or the export refuses to run.
_instance: A rule with "instance": true ships one copy of the part plus the placement of each other copy. Fasteners are the case it exists for: one M10 stud is 66,034 triangles and 519 feature edges at full resolution, and merging six of them into a budget turns the shaft faceted while pushing the edge count up to 2,050. Instanced, nothing is clustered.
_preview: A rule with "preview": false is left out of the picker model only. Threaded fasteners are three quarters of this motor's triangles and none of its silhouette; keeping them forces the decimator to tear holes in the plates to stay inside the budget, which is exactly the artefact they were meant to avoid.
_options: 'split': true makes one part per CAD instance, ordered along the axis — a stack of three identical spacer plates is three things you can point at. 'halve': 'y' cuts the merged part in two through its own centre; the grain is a tube whose bore is the point.
_angles: Dihedral angle per component model, in degrees; 30 by default. A threaded stud at 30 draws its own helix; at 70 it reduces to the hex and the chamfers.
